# TypeScript and JavaScript doc checker: survey and design

## Verdict

Build the checker as a **two-part tool**: a small Node script that extracts comments exactly (the TypeScript
compiler is already a dev dependency), and the **existing Python text rules** run over what it extracts.
That keeps one copy of the rules, which `text_rules.py` already says is the point, and it avoids writing a
TypeScript lexer in Python. The survey shows the client code is mostly `//` comments, not JSDoc, so whether
`//` comments are in scope is the biggest question and it is Rick's (question 1 below).

Population from git. The counts match Cheech's 20:35 count.

| group | files | .ts | .js / .mjs | lines |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `src/lupin_app/static` | 216 | 179 | 37 | 166,140 |
| `src/tests/unit` | 333 | 332 | 1 (.mjs) | 105,756 (the .ts files) |

## 2. Pilot: the Python rules over this text

This is a pilot, not the checker. It cuts out each JSDoc block (with the ` * ` prefixes removed) and each
`//` run, and feeds the text to `cosa.repo.doc_lint.text_rules.lint_text` as it is. The structure rules
(summary and preface length) ran on JSDoc only. Findings by rule:

| rule | static JSDoc | static `//` runs | tests JSDoc | tests `//` runs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| caps (emphasis words, glyphs not included) | 4,196 | 5,744 | 520 | 10,145 |
| sentence-length | 632 | 1,391 | 72 | 1,734 |
| bare-ref | 367 | 1,544 | 19 | 1,111 |
| glyph | 352 | 393 | 50 | 801 |
| summary-length | 580 | | 31 | |
| preface-length | 181 | | | |
| iso-date | 101 | 415 | 6 | 366 |
| tic | 140 | 154 | 21 | 283 |
| dated-banner | 38 | 135 | 1 | 68 |
| agent-imperative | 3 | 22 | | 5 |
| **total** | **6,590** | **9,798** | **720** | **14,513** |

Total 31,621 findings. Two readings:

- The most frequent caps words are `THE`, `NOT`, `IS`, `AND`, `THIS`, `ONE`, `NO`, `BEFORE`, `ONLY`: real
  shouting in prose, so the caps rule finds true cases in this code too. It also means the number is large
  because the code was written with that habit, not because the rule misfires.
- I have **not** measured the precision of these findings on TS text. The first-listed false-positive
  shapes (section 5) come from reading the Python precedents and the sample, not from a labelled set.

## 3. Rules: each Python rule mapped to its TypeScript form

Python rules live in `text_rules.py` (shared), `docstring_lint.py`, `comment_lint.py`, `links.py`.
`rule_lists.py` is frozen by ruling b42eb0de (Rick, 2026-09-30): the lists and thresholds are reused as they
are, not copied and edited.

| Python rule | TS form | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| summary-length (rule 1): first paragraph at most 90 chars | first paragraph of a JSDoc block, and the first line of a `//` header run | Same function, same limit. In JSDoc the leading `*` is stripped first. |
| blank line after summary (ruff D205) | a JSDoc block's summary followed by a blank ` *` line | ruff has no JSDoc equivalent. `eslint-plugin-jsdoc` is not installed. Cheap to add in the extractor. |
| sentence-length (rule 3): 25 words | all prose in JSDoc and in `//` runs | `//` runs are joined into paragraphs the way Python wrapped docstring lines are. |
| caps and glyphs (rule 4) | same | Needs the TS-specific exemptions of section 5. |
| tic phrases (rule 5) | same | No change; the list is frozen. |
| bare-ref (rule 6) | same | A `// row 319c57a3` style reference is common in tests (1,111 `//` hits). |
| iso-date and dated-banner (rule 7) | same | 408 + 351 `//` lines carry a date. |
| agent-imperative (rule 8) | JSDoc only is the clear case; `//` is a question | See question 2. |
| preface-length: at most 6 lines before the contract header | JSDoc with a `Requires:` / `Ensures:` / `Raises:` header | Applies only where a header exists. 181 hits in the pilot. |
| docstring-length: at most 40 lines | a JSDoc block over 40 lines | 9 blocks. For `//` runs: question 3. |
| Design: path must exist (`links.py`) | a `Design:` line in JSDoc | Same function. |
| comment_lint (`#` comments: caps, tics, history) | `//` and `/* */` comments | In Python it applies the emphasis, rhetoric and history rules only, not sentence or reference rules, "because comments hold working notes". Reuse that split for TS comments. |
| banner rule | banner lines | The docstring of `comment_lint.py` says it checks banners, but its code does not. Open: question 4. |
| parse-error finding | a file the compiler cannot parse | Same. |
| `is_tool_registered` exemption (agent-imperative off for MCP tool text) | no TS counterpart found | Nothing in the client registers text that a model reads. Say so in the checker docstring. |

### The contract

`Requires:`, `Ensures:`, `Raises:` already appear in 640 static JSDoc blocks, as in Python. `@param` is the
declared-inputs form, `@returns` is `Ensures:` for the return value, `@throws` is `Raises:`. The checker
treats **both forms as a contract** so a rewrite cannot hide a lost item inside the other form:

- `Requires:` items and `@param` lines are the "requires" side.
- `Ensures:` items and `@returns` lines are the "ensures" side.
- `Raises:` items and `@throws` lines are the "raises" side.

The Python `contract_diff.py` counts items per heading before and after and flags a vanished heading. The TS
version counts both forms per block, so changing `@param` text into a `Requires:` bullet does not show as a
loss. `@throws` has zero uses today; the check still has to understand it for new code.

## 4. The other tools around the rules

The docs sweep uses more than the linter. The TS equivalents, using the Dart tool as the model:

| Python tool | Dart precedent | TS need |
|---|---|---|
| `docstring_lint.py` | `dartdoc_lint.py`: its own lexer finds `///` blocks, then feeds `lint_text` | the extractor plus `lint_text`, section 6 |
| `docs_only_diff.py`: the AST is identical once docstrings go | Dart: every non-comment token identical, directive comments match | TS: the token list with all comments dropped is identical, the directive comments (`@ts-*`, `eslint-*`, `c8`, `istanbul`, `prettier-ignore`, `//# sourceMappingURL`, `/*! */`, `@license`) match, and **for `.js` and `.mjs` the parsed JSDoc type nodes are identical** (`ts.getJSDocTags`, each tag's `typeExpression`). The braces are type annotations that `tsc` enforces, 249 `@param`, 84 `@returns`, 11 `@type`, 6 `@typedef` in the authored `.js` files, so comparing comment text alone would let a loosened type pass |
| `contract_diff.py` | none | counts both contract forms, above |
| `*_pairs.py` (before and after text per symbol, for the claim check) | `dart_pairs.py` joins on ( file, symbol ) | `ts_pairs`: key = `( file, kind, Owner.member, ordinal )`. The file header run is `<file-header>`. Tiberius measured over 547 files: 2,338 documented nodes, 155 with no name (69 are `if` statements), 26 `Owner.member` keys that repeat (overloads, get and set pairs), hence the ordinal. Other `//` runs are **not claim-checked**: a rewrite merges or splits them, so a before and after join is undefined. They get only the reduced rule set (caps, glyph, tic, history) |
| `package_check.py` | `.py` only today | takes a TS file set and runs the four checks. Needs the TS branch. |
| claim check (`harness_cli`) | language-neutral | takes pairs, no change |

Status as of 2026-10-06 21:30 EDT: this section is specification only. Of its rows, none is built (Cheech's ruling:
no `ts_pairs`, no TS docs-only check, no TS contract check, no `package_check` TS branch tonight). What the extractor
now gives the docs-only row to compare: each tag record carries `tag`, `type`, `name` and `raw` (the tag's source
text with the star margin removed), read by the compiler for attached and stray blocks alike (commit `3e5f7e70a`),
so a nested-brace type and `@template` and `@extends` tags are compared as written.

## 5. What the checker must never flag

Predicates, not lists (the rule Cheech set on 530f1056 and 42b51734).

Precedents:

- **530f1056.** A literal configuration key such as `test fix expediter phase 1 engine = sdk | claude_code`
  was read as a bare step reference. Correct code or literal syntax is never reworded to please the lint.
- **42b51734.** `NAME` and `OUT` in a bracketed option placeholder on a usage line were read as shouting.
  The caps rule skips a caps word inside a bracketed placeholder on a usage line.
- **Related caps case** on that bug's amendment: `TaskType.BOUNDED` (an attribute access) is code.

TS and JS shapes, each as a predicate:

1. Inside a backtick span or a `{@link ...}`. (7,299 backtick spans in this code already.)
2. A JSDoc type in braces on a tag line: `@param {HTMLElement} el`, `{Map<string, Foo>}`, `{Promise<void>}`.
   Never prose; the tag line carries a type, a name and then prose.
3. An identifier that is code: any token with a dot-access (`TaskType.BOUNDED`), an underscore, a digit, or a
   call parenthesis. Same predicate as the Python rule's underscore, digit and quote exemptions.
4. A directive comment: `@ts-expect-error`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-nocheck`, `eslint-disable*`, `eslint-enable`,
   `c8 ignore`, `istanbul ignore`, `prettier-ignore`, `#region`, `/// <reference ...>`. Never findings, and a
   changed one fails the docs-only check.
5. A shebang line and a license-header block, if the file starts with one.
6. A URL (`https://...`) in a comment, a regular-expression literal inside a code span, a line inside a
   fenced or `Example:` block.
7. A `//` run that is commented-out code. Decided by parsing the whole run as a script: it is code only when
   it parses with zero diagnostics and holds a call, an assignment or a declaration. (Revised after finding
   3: my first predicate, "a line ends with `;`, `{` or `}`", hid 46 prose lines such as "Mounted BEFORE the
   task list purely to match the DOM order the user sees;".)
8. A `// @ts-expect-error` style line is only a directive when it starts the comment; the same words in the
   middle of a prose sentence are prose.
9. A file name with an extension, such as `broadcast-panel.js` in a test file's header line. A `.js`, `.ts`
   or `.md` name is a path and never counts as a bare reference.

10. In `.js` and `.mjs` files, JSDoc type syntax is code, not prose: the `{Type}` of `@param`, `@returns`,
    `@type`, `@typedef`, and the tags `@template`, `@callback`, `@satisfies`, `@this`, `@extends`, `@import`,
    `@override`. Also `//# sourceMappingURL=`, `/*! ... */` and `@license` blocks. `tsc` enforces these
    (`allowJs` and `checkJs` are on), so a docs-only change must leave them identical (section 4).

Exclusions by path: only the 2 vendored minified files (`js/vendor/marked.min.js`, `js/vendor/purify.min.js`).
The 4 `.d.ts` files are hand-written prose (113 of their 252 lines are comments) and stay in scope. See
question 5.

### Where each exemption lives (Cheech, 20:54)

**The rule: `tsdoc_lint.py` masks only shapes Python docstring text cannot have. A shape both languages have
gets no extra masking there**, so one sentence gets one verdict in both languages. The first build therefore
does not hide those shapes; where today's `text_rules.py` flags one, the finding stays, and the shape is a
proposed `text_rules.py` change for Rick (a frozen file, so Rick's word).

| shape | lives in | status |
|---|---|---|
| JSDoc type braces `{Type}` on a tag line, the tag name, the param name | TS only: masked in `tsdoc_lint.py` | in the build |
| `{@link ...}` | TS only: masked in `tsdoc_lint.py` | in the build |
| directive, `sourceMappingURL`, license block | TS only: extractor sets `directive`, no findings | in the build |
| commented-out code run | TS only: extractor sets `commented_code`, no findings | in the build |
| code span in backticks | both languages | not masked; proposed `text_rules.py` change if a rule flags text inside it (Python flags `C1` inside backticks today) |
| dotted identifier such as `TaskType.BOUNDED` | both | **already fixed in `text_rules.py` at `8f29dd7e2`** (caps skips an enum member); the TS path gets it through the shared rules, with no masking in `tsdoc_lint.py` |
| bracketed option placeholder on a usage line | both | **already fixed in `text_rules.py` at `224eec7eb`** (bug 42b51734: caps skips the placeholder after a command-line option); `Usage: [--json NONE]` is not flagged, and the TS path gets it through the shared rules |
| `key = value` literal line | both | **already fixed in `text_rules.py` at `5d8f09e81`** (step words in a config key) |
| URL | both | proposed `text_rules.py` change |
| fenced block or `Example:` block | both | proposed `text_rules.py` change |
| file name ending in `.js`, `.ts`, `.md` | both | proposed `text_rules.py` change |

The shared-shape rows are filled in from the build's report of which of them `text_rules.py` flags today.
A test feeds the same sentence through the Python docstring path and the TS comment path and requires the
same findings from both.

## 6. Architecture

### Recommended: Node extractor, Python rules

1. `src/scripts/ts_doc_extract.mjs`, run with the repo's `typescript`, prints JSON lines, one process per
   package and not per file: for each comment `{ file, kind: "jsdoc" | "block" | "line-run" | "trailing",
   text, start_line, end_line, symbol_key, directive: bool, tags: [...], ts_version }`. It uses
   `ts.createSourceFile`, then `getLeadingCommentRanges` and `getTrailingCommentRanges` at every node's full
   start and end. A bare `ts.createScanner` loop is not enough: it cannot tell division from a regular-expression
   literal or a template continuation, because the parser drives those re-scans (Tiberius, finding 2).
   Tiberius ran this route over all 216 static files: 0 parse errors, 2,055 JSDoc blocks. The TypeScript
   version is stamped into the output, because `package.json` carries a caret range (`^5.7.2`), so counts are
   reproducible. Golden fixtures for the cases that break the naive route: `/ab+\/\//`, a template with
   `${ /* c */ }`, `a / b // c`, `x = /re/g // trailing`, a hashbang, an HTML-style `<!--` comment.
2. `src/cosa/repo/doc_lint/tsdoc_lint.py` calls the extractor, strips the JSDoc `*` prefixes, joins `//`
   runs, applies the exemptions of section 5 as predicates, and calls `lint_text`. Same finding shape, same
   `run_linter` entry point, same CLI.
3. `ts_pairs.py`, the docs-only token check and the contract check follow in section 4.

Why this over the alternatives:

| option | for | against |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Node extractor, Python rules (recommended)** | one copy of the rules, no drift; exact comment boundaries | two processes; the extractor is a TypeScript or ESM file that needs its own 100% coverage under c8 |
| B. Pure-Python lexer, as for Dart | one process, stdlib only, can be vendored | a regex or lexer for `/` (division against a regular-expression literal), template strings and JSX is where the Dart lexer needed most of its 197 lines; a wrong boundary is a wrong finding |
| C. The checker written in TypeScript with its own rule copy | one language, fits `eslint` | a second implementation of every rule, and `text_rules.py` already records why that is wrong. The frozen word list would need a copy |

Tests, as the 100% mandate and Cheech's brief require: Python lines, branches and functions at 100% for the
new `.py` files; c8 `--100` for the `.mjs`. One unit test per rule on a minimal TS snippet, and for each rule
a **redden proof** that deletes the rule's check and watches the named test fail. A fixture per section 5
exemption in both directions (the shape alone gives 0 findings; the same words in prose still fire). At least
one fixture captured from a real client file through the real extractor, not hand-written.

Where it runs: `package_check` for a TS package, and `src/tests/run-typecheck-gate.sh` is the model for a
fast gate. It is not wired as a merge gate in this build.

### Test seam and shared exemptions (Tiberius, finding 6)

- The Python unit tier must not need Node. `tsdoc_lint.py` is tested against extractor **JSON fixtures**, one of
  them captured through the real extractor. The `.mjs` extractor is tested in the TypeScript tier (c8
  `--100`). One end-to-end run through both goes in a scheduled tier. The c8 include set must cover
  `src/scripts/*.mjs`; `package.json` has no c8 config, so the build adds it.
- **The exemptions live in `text_rules.py`, not in `tsdoc_lint.py`.** Masking backticks only on the TS side
  would give one text two verdicts: Python's `reference_findings` flags `C1` inside backticks today.
  Where an exemption is wanted for both languages (the 530f1056 and 42b51734 predicates) it is written once,
  in `text_rules.py`, and the Python tests cover both directions. Whether Python's backtick behaviour changes
  is a separate decision (question 9).

**Build constraint (Cheech, 20:53): `text_rules.py` and `rule_lists.py` are not edited in this build, and no
client `.ts` or `.js` file is touched.** So the first build puts the TS-only exemptions in `tsdoc_lint.py`, as
masking applied to the text before `lint_text` runs (shared shapes are not masked; see "Where each exemption
lives"). That keeps the frozen files frozen and means the Python
side keeps flagging a label inside backticks (question 9 stays open). The cost is the one Tiberius named: two
places decide what is exempt. `tsdoc_lint.py` therefore marks each masking function with the `text_rules`
behaviour it differs from, so a later move into `text_rules.py` is a cut and paste, not a redesign.

### Extractor output, the contract between the two parts

`node src/scripts/ts_doc_extract.mjs --repo-root <dir> <repo-relative file>...` prints JSON Lines:

- one `{ "kind": "file", "file", "ts_version", "parse_errors": [ { "line", "message" } ] }` per file, and
- one object per comment: `{ "kind": "jsdoc" | "block" | "line-run" | "trailing", "file", "text",
  "start_line", "end_line", "symbol_key", "directive", "tags", "ts_version" }`.

`text` is the comment body with the delimiters and the leading ` * ` or `//` removed, lines joined by a
newline. A `line-run` is consecutive leading `//` comments on consecutive lines, merged. `symbol_key` is
`<file-header>`, or `<kind>|<Owner.member>|<ordinal>`, or `null` for a run that attaches to nothing.
`directive` is true for the section 5 item 4 forms. `tags` holds `{ "tag", "type", "name" }` from
`ts.getJSDocTags` (`type` is the type expression text or `null`).

## 7. Questions that are Rick's

Each has a recommendation. None blocks the build of the rule engine; they change what it reports on.

1. **Are `//` comments in scope, or only JSDoc?** Counts: 9,361 `//` runs and 32,534 `//` lines against 2,355
   JSDoc blocks. Python's `comment_lint` is the model: `#` comments get the emphasis, tic and history rules
   but not the sentence and reference rules. Recommended: apply that reduced set to `//` comments and the
   full set to JSDoc. If out: the checker covers 2,355 blocks and tests' headers go unseen.
2. **Does the agent-imperative rule apply to TS comments?** In Python a docstring can reach a model.
   Client code reaches no model, so the three static JSDoc hits and 27 `//` hits (`Don't ...`) read as plain
   instructions to a person. Recommended: apply to JSDoc only, or drop it for TS.
3. **A length cap for `//` file headers?** 451 + 501 runs are over 6 lines, the test headers go to 128 lines.
   They carry the "why this file exists" reasoning. Recommended: no cap on `//` runs, since the Python rule
   caps docstrings, not comments.
4. **Banners** (933 + 1,985 lines of `// ----` rules and section markers). Python's comment_lint does not
   test them in code. Recommended: leave them alone; they are layout, not prose.
5. **Exclusions:** the 2 vendored minified files. Recommended: exclude them by path. Keep the 4 `.d.ts`
   files in scope; they are hand-written (Tiberius, finding 5; my first draft excluded them).
6. **Thresholds:** reuse 90 / 25 / 6 / 40 as they are. Recommended yes. The lists are frozen by ruling
   b42eb0de, so a change needs Rick's word anyway.
7. **Enforcement:** warn mode (as the Python commit hook runs today) or a blocking gate, and when.
   Recommended: warn mode until a JS/TS sweep has been ruled (D14, R.10), since 31,621 pilot findings would
   block every TS commit.
8. **Dates in comments** (759 `//` lines with ISO dates). The history rule would move them to commit bodies,
   a sweep decision. Recommended: the checker reports them; nothing rewrites them in this task.
9. **Backticks and the reference rule.** `reference_findings` flags `C1` inside backticks today, and the
   exemption lists in section 5 want code spans exempt. Recommended: exempt a bare label inside a code span
   in `text_rules.py` for both languages, with tests both ways. It changes Python findings, so it is Rick's.
10. **Test file headers as documents.** Tiberius: a test file's `//` header is a document and gets the
    summary and history rules, not only the reduced set. Recommended: yes, for the 332 headers.

## 8. What I did not measure, and where this could mislead

For Tiberius's critique, the places I think a wrong answer could look right:

- **The counts come from a regex scan, not the compiler.** A `/**` inside a string, a template literal or a
  regular expression would count as a JSDoc block. The scan found 20 + 62 code lines with `http://` in a
  string; none were checked for a `/*` inside. The extractor in the design is built to remove this error,
  and the first test of it is to rerun these counts through it and compare.
- **"Directly above a declaration"** used a pattern of the next 200 characters, so a JSDoc above a decorator
  or an overload counts as floating. 195 floating is an upper bound.
- **The pilot's findings are not precision-checked.** The text was cut with a regex, `//` runs include any
  commented-out code (170 lines), and the sentence rule ran over joined runs that may hold lists. Nobody
  labelled a sample.
- **`@throws` zero is a count of the text `@throws`.** A throws clause written as `Raises:` is counted under
  Raises.
- **The seat tree is at `aa4b7d6e0`**, older than main. The population count matched Cheech's at main at
  20:35, so the file set agrees; the comment counts were not re-run at main.
- **Not looked at:** the `.html` files under static (35) with inline `<script>` and `<style>`; they hold JS
  that this checker would not see. `src/rnd/...mjs` probes and `src/websocket_smoke` TS (2 files) are outside
  the two groups.
- **Not run at all:** the extractor, the compiler's scanner, any real TS checker. No file under
  `src/lupin_app/static` or `src/tests/unit` was changed.
